newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy's Savio says cancels its public share offer.
newsitem.headline: Italy's Savio says cancels its public share offer.

text.p: Italian textile machinery group Savio Macchine Tessile SpA said it had cancelled its initial public offer (IPO) of shares due on November 28 and November 29 after unsatisfactory bookbuilding.

Savio, which is a world leader in the production of yarn finishing machines, had decided to seek a stock exchange listing at its shareholders meeting in July with a market offer of over 40 percent of its capital.

The company said in a statement that it had decided to put off the share offer after examining the result of bookbuilding with institutional investors which closed Tuesday morning with its joint global co-ordinators Schroders and Banca Commerciale Italiana.
It added that the group would put off the share offer until after the publication of the company's final financial results for the current year.

Savio had been part of state energy group ENI before being acquired by a group of financial investors and managers in June 1995. The company turned in a gross profit of 22 billion lire on a turnover of 267 billion lire in 1995.
